excerpt: வீடு விட்டு ஓடிப்போன வடிவேலரே நீ படும்

sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
வீடு விட்டு ஓடிப்போன வடிவேலரே நீ படும்
பாடு பற்றி பாடுதையா இந்த நாடே (ஓ முருகய்யே)
sections.translit:
vIdu vittu OdippOna vadivElarE nI padum
pAdu patRi pAdudhaiyA indha nAdE (O MurugayyE)
sections.en: Oh Muruga, You ran away from home. The whole country is talking about the tribulations you are facing.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
கால் ஆடையும் கைத்தடியும் பால் நீறும் பூண்டே
மால் மருகா மலையுச்சியில் நின்றிடவே வேகமாக
sections.translit:
kAl Adaiyum kaitthadiyum pAl nIRum pUNdE
mAl marugA malaiyucchiyil nindRidavE vEgamAga
sections.en: Look at your appearance with scant clothing on your body, a stick in your hand and sacred ash on your forehead. Oh nephew of Vishnu, you left in such a hurry to find a place on a mere hill top.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
கனி ஒன்றுக்காக முனி செய்த சதியாலே சினம் கொண்டே
நீல மயில் மீதேறி ஞாலவலம் வந்த போதும்
இடும்பனின் காவடியில் அடங்கிப்போன கடம்பசாமி இறுதியாக
அம்மையப்பன் வீட்டில் தானே செம்மையாகச் சென்றமர்ந்தாய்
எம்மையாளும் ஈசனின்றி ஓரணுவும் அசையாதென்னும்
ஊரறிந்த உண்மையை நீ மறந்ததென்னே
sections.translit:
kani ondRukkAga muni seydha sadhiyAlE sinam koNdE
nIla mayil mIdhERi nyAlavalam vandha pOdhum
idumbanin kAvadiyil adangippOna kadambasAmi iRudhiyAga
ammaiyappan vIttil thAnE semmaiyAgach chendRamarndhAy
emmaiyALum IsanindRi OraNuvum asaiyAdhennum
UraRindha uNmaiyai nI maRandhadhennE
sections.en: You became furious at the evil plot of Sage Narada and succumbed to the fruit which you were hoping to win as a contest prize. You climbed at once on your blue peacock and went around the world. Kadamba flower wearing Lord Muruga, you calmed down with the devotion of the demon Idumban carrying a Kavadi of the two hills on his shoulders. Finally, you settled down comfortably on the twin peaks of Kailash, your father’s abode. It is all preordained. Not even a miniscule size atom will budge without the ordain from your father, Lord Siva. The entire world knows this eternal truth. Did you forget this maxim?

notes: This song was specially composed for the author’s daughter, Priti Radhakrishnan, on the occasion of a Bharatanatyam recital. This recital was a fundraiser for the Siva Murugan Temple in Concord, California. Under the expert guidance of her Guru, Smt. Mythili Kumar, Priti performed this piece along with another song entitled “Umaiyoru Pangan Endru”. Rooted in classical mythology, the song narrates the well-known tale of the contest between Lord Muruga and his brother, Lord Ganesha, where they both sought the prized fruit. When Sage Narada presented a sacred fruit to Lord Shiva and Parvati, their sons were told that whoever circles the world fastest shall receive the fruit. Muruga set off on his peacock to circumnavigate the globe, but Ganesha simply walked around his parents, declaring that they represented his entire world. He won the fruit. Upon returning and discovering the outcome, Muruga became disheartened and, in his frustration, departed from his celestial home, eventually reaching the sacred hills of Palani. Lines 3 and 4 of the charanam of the song refers to the Kavadi tradition and the touching story of Idumban, whose unwavering devotion impressed Muruga. The irony noted by the poet lies in Muruga ultimately choosing to dwell in Sivagiri and Sakthigiri, the very hills symbolically tied to his parents’ home on Mount Kailash. Legend of the Kavadi: There is a legend associated with the ritual of carrying a Kavadi. Lord Siva once instructed Sage Agasthiya to proceed southward. The sage, being a devout worshipper of Siva and Parvathi, was reluctant to leave the sacred Sivagiri and Sakthigiri hills in Kailash. To continue his worship in the south, he decided to move the divine hills there. The poet sarcastically notes that Muruga would ultimately settle down in the home of his parents, as it was preordained by the Supreme Siva. Agasthiya assigned this task of carrying the two Kailash hills to his disciple Idumban, a demon who had survived the war between Lord Muruga and Surapadman. Idumban and his wife Idumbi, having become devotees of Muruga after the war, gladly accepted the mission. After praying to Lord Siva, Idumban obtained a powerful staff, rumored to be as strong as the Brahma Danda. Siva also provided serpents from eight directions, which Idumban used as ropes to tie the two hills to either end of his staff, creating a balance-like structure: the Kavadi. With this, they carried the hills on their shoulders. When Idumban reached Thiru Avinankudi (the scriptural name for Palani), he became exhausted and set the Kavadi down. There, he encountered a young boy sitting on one of the hills. He asked the boy to leave, unaware that this was Muruga himself, who had recently left home after a dispute with his parents and elder brother over a prized fruit. Still angered by the outcome of the contest, Muruga refused to leave. A battle ensued in which Muruga killed Idumban. Recognizing the boy as Lord Muruga, Idumbi implored him to restore Idumban’s life. Moved by her devotion, Muruga revived Idumban and blessed them both. Idumban asked to remain as the eternal guardian of the Palani Hills. He requested that any devotee in the future who climbs the hills carrying a Kavadi, with offerings and worship items for Muruga, be granted eternal joy and prosperity. Muruga granted this wish and gave them another boon: anyone who prays at the Idumban shrine, located halfway up the hills, will be considered as having worshipped Muruga himself and will receive His full grace and compassion. The details of Muruga residing in Siva Giri and Sakthi Giri can be found in the sthalapuranam of the temple based on the famous composition by Balasubramania Kavirayar in the year 1628AD, which contains 987 verses and 23 chapters. பழநித் தல வரலாறு, அருள்மிகு தண்டாயுதபாணி சுவாமி திருக்கோயில், பழனி – 624601, திண்டுக்கல் மாவட்டம், பதிப்பாசிரியர்: முனைவர் இரத்தின. கிருட்டிணமூர்த்தி, திருத்திய பன்னிரண்டாம் பதிப்பு, ஜனவரி 2005, பக்கங்கள்: 3, 25, 35 – 38, 45 – 46, 48 – 50, 52 – 55.
